info.name: Steam Web API
info.description:
Steam Web API — manual API testing collection

Scope: six requests against the public Steam Web API, covering positive, negative,  
boundary and parameter-effect checks on two endpoints (ISteamUserStats, ISteamNews).

Why this API: it is publicly documented and several of its methods work without an  
API key, so the expected behaviour of each response is defined and can be asserted  
against. Undocumented endpoints were deliberately avoided — without a specification  
there is no oracle, and an expected result would have to be invented.

Environment: the `baseUrl` variable holds [https://api.steampowered.com](https://api.steampowered.com). No credentials  
are stored in this collection. If an API key is ever added, it must be stored as a  
`secret` variable and never committed to the repository.

Response time policy: every request asserts a response time below 10000 ms. This is a  
clearly-abnormal ceiling, not a performance requirement — no response-time SLA has been  
agreed for this API, so a stricter threshold would be an invented expectation. A genuine  
performance threshold would need to be defined with the team.

Rate limits: requests that produce HTTP 403 can lead to the client IP being temporarily  
blocked. This collection is intended for manual runs; do not loop it in the Collection  
Runner.

Observations recorded during testing:

1. Successful responses are returned as JSON, but error responses (for example, a missing  
    required parameter) are returned as HTML. Clients therefore have to parse two different  
    formats. No documented requirement covers this, so it is recorded as a question rather  
    than a defect.
    
2. ISteamApps/GetAppList/v2 returns 404 with the message "Method 'GetAppList' not found in  
    interface 'ISteamApps'". The official documentation marks this method as deprecated in  
    favour of IStoreService/GetAppList, which requires an API key. The endpoint was replaced  
    in this collection by ISteamUserStats/GetGlobalAchievementPercentagesForApp.

exec: pm.test("Response time is under 10000 ms", function () {
pm.test("player_count is a non-negative number", function () {

request.description:
Positive scenario for GetNumberOfCurrentPlayers.

What: requests the current player count for a valid appid (730 — Counter-Strike 2).  
Why: verifies the response contract — player_count present, numeric, non-negative,  
and result equal to 1.  
Note: the player count changes constantly, so the test asserts type and range rather  
than a specific value.

exec: pm.test("Response time is under 10000 ms", function () {
pm.test("Body is JSON with response.result", function () {
pm.test("result is not the success code", function () {
pm.test("No player_count for an unknown appid", function () {

request.description:
Negative scenario for GetNumberOfCurrentPlayers.

What: requests the player count for an appid that does not exist (999999999).  
Why: verifies that an unknown appid produces an explicit failure rather than an empty  
success response — status 404, a non-success result code, and no player_count field.  
Note: this endpoint has shown occasional slow responses on unknown appids. A single slow  
run is not a finding; re-run before treating it as one.

exec: pm.test("Response time is under 10000 ms", function () {
pm.test("Error message names the missing parameter", function () {

request.description:
Negative scenario: a required parameter is omitted.

What: calls GetNumberOfCurrentPlayers without the appid parameter.  
Why: verifies that the API rejects the request with a 4xx status and names the missing  
parameter in the error message, rather than returning 200 or 500.  
Note: the error body is returned as HTML, not JSON. The test therefore uses  
pm.response.text() — calling pm.response.json() on this response would throw, and the  
test would fail because of the script, not because of the API.

exec: pm.test("Response time is under 10000 ms", function () {
pm.test("Response appid matches the requested appid", function () {
pm.test("newsitems length equals the requested count", function () {

request.description:
Parameter-effect scenario for GetNewsForApp.

What: requests news entries for appid 730 with count=3.  
Why: verifies that the count parameter is honoured — the newsitems array holds exactly  
the requested number of entries.  
Note: the count field inside the response body is the total number of news entries  
available for the app, not the number returned. The assertion uses newsitems.length.

exec: pm.test("Response time is under 10000 ms", function () {
pm.test("Response appid matches the requested appid", function () {
pm.test("newsitems is empty when count=0", function () {

request.description:
Boundary value for the count parameter of GetNewsForApp.

What: requests news entries for appid 730 with count=0.  
Why: verifies that the lower boundary is handled as a valid request — status 200 with an  
empty newsitems array — rather than as an error or as a default-sized response.

exec: pm.test("Response time is under 10000 ms", function () {
pm.test("Body is JSON with expected properties", function () {
pm.test("Types of achievements entries are correct", function () {
pm.test("Percent value is within 0 and 100", function () {

request.description:
Response contract for GetGlobalAchievementPercentagesForApp.

What: requests global achievement completion percentages for gameid 730.  
Why: verifies the structure of a nested response — achievements is a non-empty array and  
each entry carries name and percent.  
Note 1: percent is returned as a string, not a number. Type and value are therefore  
asserted separately: the type check records the actual contract, the range check (0-100)  
records the meaning.  
Note 2: the parameter-effect layer does not apply to this request. The response does not  
echo gameid, so there is nothing in the body to compare the request parameter against.  
Asserting anything here would produce a test that can never fail.  
Note 3: this request replaced ISteamApps/GetAppList/v2, which now returns 404 and is  
marked deprecated in the official documentation.
